Then, as the prince went along the road, he gradually beheld
an old man — his trembling hand placed on a staff, beauty departed,
with an extremely white head,
with a stooped body, as if fashioned by the pure [state of] abiding [of old age].

children.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sārathim apṛcchat kathaya tāvat kaḥ punar ayam āropitadhanurānataparidurbalāṅgaḥ pariṇatakāśakusumasitaśirasijaḥ śiraḥprakampeṇa kim api pralayann ivālokyate | sārathir uvāca | kumāra jarā nāma sarvalokavyāpinī śarīrendriyapāṭavahāriṇī madanakathātiraskaraṇī kupiteva yūnām yauvanamadam utsārayati yayaiṣa imām avasthāṃ nīta iti | atha sa mahātmā punar uvāca | yadi jarā tāruṇyam evaṃ vināśayati kā nāma ratir asmin pariṇāmini dehe | sūta uvāca | kumāra na kevalaṃ jarā vyādhir api dhātukṣobhasaṃbhūto dehināṃ mahān anarthaḥ | tato 'paro mṛtyur nāma sarvakriyāpaharaṇapaṭur anarthataro yaḥ paricintyamāno 'pi śarīriṇāṃ mahad duḥkham utpādayati | bodhisattva uvāca |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> asked his charioteer: 'Tell me, who is this person — his body stooped and extremely weak like a bow that has been strung, his hair on his head white as the flower of ripe <s>kāśa</s> grass, seemingly muttering something with the trembling of his head?' The charioteer said: 'Prince, it is old age (<s>jarā</s>) — pervading the entire world, robbing the body and senses of their vigor, the overthrower of tales of love-passion — as if angered, it expels the pride of youth from the young. By it, this man has been brought to this condition.' Then that great-souled one spoke again: 'If old age thus destroys youth, what delight can there be in this body subject to transformation?' The charioteer said: 'Prince, not only old age — disease too, arising from the disturbance of the bodily humors, is a great calamity for embodied beings. And beyond that, there is death, skilled in taking away all activities, an even greater misfortune, which, even when merely contemplated, produces great suffering in embodied beings.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:
'Alas, this world is pursued day after day
by these three enemies — death, disease, and old age;'
'yet in the presence of such terrible danger,
how is it devoted solely to sense-pleasures?'
'Therefore, O charioteer, turn the chariot back swiftly!
Go to the house! What is the point of lingering here?'
'For me who dreads death, disease, and old age,
there will be no delight in the pleasure-garden!'

children.text: atha rājā saṃvignamanasaṃ bodhisattvaṃ śrutvā tāṃ cāsitasya vācam anusmṛtya bhaviṣyattanayaviyogāśaṅkitamanāḥ sārathaye saṃdideśa | pramadavanam eva kumāro netavya iti | sa ca sārathiḥ prasabham enam upavanam eva praviśyābhihitavān | draṣṭum arhaty āyuṣmān iha hi |
children.translated_text: Then the king, hearing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s stirred mind, and recalling <s>Asita</s>'s words, with his mind apprehensive about the future separation from his son, instructed the charioteer: 'The prince is to be taken to the pleasure-garden only!' And that charioteer, forcing him to enter the garden itself, said: 'May the long-lived one deign to behold [this] — for here:'
'Gradually, gradually revealing the beauty of their flower-smiles,
gently, gently set to dancing by the <s>Malaya</s> breeze as it glides —'
'the slender maiden-creepers of the garden shine,
with braids of buzzing bee-rows jingling at their edges!'

children.text:
atha bodhisattvo rathād avatīrya jarāmaraṇarogacintāparyākulamatir antaḥśalya iva dviradapatir ity abravīt |
dhairyacchidas
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, descending from the chariot, his mind distraught with thoughts of old age, death, and disease, like an elephant-lord with an [arrow-]thorn within, spoke: 'Those that shatter steadfastness,
that are distasteful in their end for those of feeble mind —
fierce as serpents, shunned by the tranquil-souled —'
'the sense-objects, enemies of the world, rivals even of a youth subject to desire —

children.text: paryākulaṃ na hi mano viṣayā haranti
children.translated_text: they do not carry away the agitated mind!'

children.text:
atha sa rājā nṛttagītakuśalāḥ prakāśāṅganā bodhisattvahṛdayāpakarṣaṇāya tad upavanam prāhiṇot | tāś ca kumāram abhigamya madajanitaprāgalbhyās tāṃ tāṃ ceṣṭām āviścakruḥ | atha kācid enam uktavatī paśya kumāra |
vānty
children.translated_text: Then the king sent courtesans skilled in dance and song to the garden, to captivate the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s heart. And they, approaching the prince, with boldness born of passion, displayed various gestures. Then one said to him: 'Behold, O prince!'
'These fragrant <s>Malaya</s> breezes blow, shaking the flower-trees;
a bee circumambulates the just-sprouting mango cluster;'
'while you stand composed — as if [not noticing the] long cord [being] strung upon [<s>Kāma</s>'s] bow —
the <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) calls with a piercing note — I suspect it is urging the flower-bowed [Cupid]!'
And furthermore:
'This young maiden, the mango-blossom girl, her body-paint made of her own pollen —

children.text: bhramaravareṇa bhramatā kṣaṇam iva parihīyate tanvī //
children.translated_text: she is being, as it were, ravished in a moment by the roving lord of bees, the slender one.'
Another then said to him:
'Seeing the bee — the husband of the creeper-women — who has enjoyed [them]
and is dusted gray with their flower-pollen —'
'the lotus-pool, with its young lotuses swaying in the breeze,
seems to threaten [him] again and again!'
Another said to him:

children.text: gacchāmy ahaṃ tava kṛte kusumāni yāvad
children.translated_text: 'I am going to fetch flowers for you,
these [flowers] dense with fine nectar —'
'O prince, please drive away from a distance, in the meantime,
this restless, two-winged [bee] that obstructs my gaze!'

children.text: aparā punaḥ sahāsam abhitaḥ sthitvainam abhyadhāt |
children.translated_text: Another, standing close by with a laugh, said to him:
'Having shaken the bakula-bow-string from which a bee has dislodged the stamens,
and placing upon your chest the floral bow — its shadow white as conch-shell fragments —'

children.text: gāmbhīryād avadhīrayantam abalās tvām ājighāṃsuḥ smaraḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Smara</s> (Cupid), wishing to strike you, a woman, who disregard [him] from [your] depth —
is surely straightening his floral arrow, with one eye closed [to aim]!'

children.text: bodhisattva uvāca | alam alaṃ bhaginya ebhir asatpralāpaiḥ | na khalu mama saṃvigne manasi saliladhārā iva hutabhuji śṛṅgārakathāḥ samavakāśam adhunā labhante |
children.translated_text: The Bodhisattva said: 'Enough, enough of these improper utterances, O sister! Indeed, in my agitated mind, amorous tales find no more place now than streams of water upon a blazing fire.'
Hearing that word 'sister' from him,
the women
lowered their faces,
their flirtations abandoned by shame.
Seeing that host of young women embarrassed,
and the prince of pure mind spiritually agitated,
<s>Smara</s> (Cupid), placing his floral arrows back in the quiver,
abashedly lowered his bow.

children.text: atha bodhisattvas tatra pramadavane ratim alabhamāno 'stam upeyuṣi savitari rathavaram adhiruhya tāś cāṅganā bhavanam ājagmuḥ | tato bodhisattvaḥ śṛṅgārakathām avamanyamānaḥ śayanatale viniviśya jarāmaraṇarogān eva manasi nidhāya cintāparo babhūva | tataḥ śuddhāvāsais tasya mahātmanaḥ saṃvejanāya śayanapālikānām sadya eva nidrāvaktavyatā kriyate sma | tatra ca kāsāṃcid aviralaśabdaśvāsavaśaprakāśadaśanāni vigalitalālālavavyāptaparyantāni vadanāny abhūvan | anparāsāṃ ca kuṭṭimatalaparyastāni praśithilavigalitadukūlatayā pravyaktorūṇi payodharoparivyavakīrṇahārāṇi nikṣiptaviṣamabhujalatāni mṛtānām iva śarīrāṇy āsan | aparā ca murajapuṣkaraviniveśitadviguṇabāhūpadhānavinihitānanā viṣṭarād vinipatya tathaiva śiṣye | kasyāścin nidrāpahṛtāṅguliyatnāt karād adharaviśliṣṭaprathamarandhraḥ pramadānayanatārakānīlo vaṃśaḥ papāta |
dviradaviloḍitānām iva kamalinīnāṃ vividhāvasthaṃ tāsāṃ ca rūpam ālokya hasitam iva yaṣṭipradīpaiḥ
children.translated_text: And seeing their appearances in these various states, like lotus-beds churned by elephants, the lamp-on-a-staff seemed to laugh at them.

children.text: | atha bodhisattvas tāsām yuvatīnāṃ nindāṃ kṛtvābhyutthāya niṣkramya cchandakam utthāpyovāca |
children.translated_text: Then the Bodhisattva, having expressed contempt for those young women, arose and went out, awakened <s>Chandaka</s>, and said:

Then the Bodhisattva, finding no delight in that pleasure garden, when the sun had set, mounted the excellent chariot and those women returned to the palace. Then the Bodhisattva, disdaining amorous talk, lying upon his bed, fixing his mind only on old age, death, and disease, became absorbed in contemplation. Then the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) deities, for the spiritual awakening of that great soul, instantly induced sleep upon the chamber-attendants. And the faces of some women were exposed — their teeth visible through the force of audible breathing, their surroundings covered with trickles of escaped saliva. The bodies of others lay sprawled upon the floor, their fine garments loosened and slipping, exposing their thighs, their necklaces scattered over their breasts, their arm-creepers cast about crookedly — like the bodies of the dead. Another, having fallen from her couch, lay just as she was, her face resting upon her doubled arms placed as pillows upon a <s>muraja</s> drum. From the hand of one, the effort of whose fingers was stolen by sleep, a flute fell — blue as the pupils of the ladies' eyes — slipping from her lips' first opening.
'Intending to cross this ocean of worldly existence,
I am resolved to go to the forest of austerities.
Therefore, for the accomplishment of my resolve,
bring the swift horse <s>Kanthaka</s>.'

children.text:
chandakaś ca śuddhādhivāsaiś codyamānas tad rājaśāsanam anādṛtya tatheti pratiśrutya vāmakakṣyāvinihitāsiḥ kanthakam aśvavaram āninā-
ya | bodhisattvādhirūḍhaṃ tam aśvaṃ paścād vadhryāvalambinā cchandakena saha yakṣakumārāḥ karatalavinihitakhuraṃ prabhātasamaye nabhasā maharṣer arāḍasyāśramasamīpam avatārayāmāsur iti |
children.translated_text: And <s>Chandaka</s>, urged by the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> deities, disregarding the royal command, consented saying 'So be it,' and placing a sword at his left side, brought the excellent horse <s>Kanthaka</s>. And the <s>Yakṣa</s> youths, bearing in their palms the hooves of that horse mounted by the Bodhisattva, with <s>Chandaka</s> following behind holding the girth-strap, brought them down from the sky at dawn near the hermitage of the great sage <s>Arāḍa</s>.
Then, removing from his body the ornaments
that blazed with the brilliance of bright gems,
he slowly cut with a sword his locks of hair,
dark as the throat of a cuckoo, rippling like river-waves.
Seeing him stripped of his ornaments, <s>Chandaka</s>,
like a clear lake from which the lotuses have been taken away,
tormented by the blazing fire of powerful grief,
shed tear-drops resembling pearls.

children.text: bodhisattva uvāca | na khalu dharmonmukhe suhṛdi svajane vā tapovanābhiprasthite viṣādaṃ kartum arhati sajjanaḥ | tad gaccha mama gurujanam evaṃ brūhi |
children.translated_text: The Bodhisattva said: 'Indeed, a good person ought not to despair when a friend or kinsman, turning toward <s>Dharma</s>, sets out for the forest of austerities. Go, and speak thus to my elders:'
'Either this body of mine shall be worn away
by intense austerities,
or I shall attain that state
which has been seen by the seers of truth.'

children.text: chandakaś ca tatheti bodhisattvam abhipraṇamyāśvam ābharaṇāni cādāya krameṇa nagaram āgamya taṃ bodhisattvasaṃdeśaṃ narapataye nivedayāmāsa | śrutvā ca tasya viniścayaṃ sahāntaḥpureṇa śuddhodano bahuvidhaṃ vilalāpa | bodhisattvaś ca lubdhakarūpadhāriṇo devaputrāt svena śaśikiraṇarucinā vasanayugena kāṣāye vāsasī krītvā paridhāya śanaiḥ śanair arāḍasyāśramaṃ jagāma | dṛṣṭvā ca bodhisattvam āgacchantam arāḍaḥ svāgataṃ svāgatam ity abhidhāya svam uṭajam ānīya vetrāsane samupaveśya kuśalapūrvakam ālāpaṃ cakāra | tato bodhisattvas tam apṛcchat |
children.translated_text: And <s>Chandaka</s>, saying 'So be it,' bowed deeply to the Bodhisattva and, taking the horse and the ornaments, gradually returned to the city and conveyed that message of the Bodhisattva to the king. And <s>Śuddhodana</s>, hearing of his resolve, lamented in many ways together with the inner chambers. And the Bodhisattva, from a divine being (<s>Devaputra</s>) in the form of a hunter, purchased saffron robes with his own pair of garments, radiant as moonbeams, and donning them, slowly proceeded to the hermitage of <s>Arāḍa</s>. And seeing the Bodhisattva approaching, <s>Arāḍa</s>, saying 'Welcome, welcome!' brought him to his hut, seated him on a wicker seat, and engaged in conversation beginning with pleasantries. Then the Bodhisattva asked him:
'What is the nature of your <s>Dharma</s>?
And how is it to be realized?
To me, who desires to see the truth,
may the best of beings deign to speak.'

children.text: arāḍa uvāca | śrotum arhati mahābhāga iti | prakṛtivikārayor janmajarāmṛtyavas tattvam ity abhihitam | prakṛtiś ca pañca mahābhūtāny ahaṃkāro vyaktaṃ ceti | vikāraś cendriyāṇi tadarthāś ca pāṇipādavākpāyūpasthaṃ mana ity asya kṣetraṃ vijānāti | tat kṣetrajña ity abhidhīyate | kṣetrajñaṃ cātmānam avacakṣate tattvavidaḥ | yac cotpādāvasānān maraṇadharmātmakaṃ tad vyaktam iti boddhavyam avyaktam etadviparyayād iti | ajñānaṃ karma tṛṣṇā ca saṃsārahetavo vijñeyāḥ | tritaye cāvasthito jantur na sattvam atikramya vartate | vipratyayāhaṃkārasaṃdehābhisaṃplavāviśeṣānupāyasaṅgābhyavapātāḥ | vipratyayo nāma viparītapravartanam | aham abhidadhāmy ahaṃ vedmīty evamādy ahaṃkāraḥ | yas tv asaṃdigdhān api bhāvān mṛtpiṇḍavad ekībhāvena paśyati sa saṃdeha iti mantavyaḥ | yad eva cāhaṃ tāny evāmūni manobuddhikarmāṇi | yaś caiṣa gaṇaḥ so 'ham ity abhisaṃplavam udāharanti | aviśeṣaḥ punaḥ pratibuddhāpratibuddhayor aviśeṣajñatā prakṛtīnāṃ ca so 'viśeṣa iti boddhavyaḥ | svāhākāravaṣaṭkāraprokṣaṇābhyukṣaṇādayo hy anupāya iti boddhavyaḥ | yatra vastuni saktim upety amedhā manovāgbuddhikarmabhiḥ so 'bhiṣvaṅga ity abhidhīyate | mamedam asyāham iti yad duḥkham abhimanyate so 'bhyavapātaḥ | prāṇināṃ saṃsārahetur ālasyaṃ nāma | tamo moho mṛtyujanmanī | mahāmohaḥ kāma iti saṃjñitaḥ | tāmisraṃ ca krodha ity avagamyatām | viṣādaḥ punar andhatāmisram abhidhīyate | anayāvidyayā pañcaparvayā bāliśo baddhamanā jātyādau mahati duḥkhe punaḥ punar āvartate | tatra cāhaṃ draṣṭā śrotā mantā kāryakāraṇaṃ cety evam avagamya saṃsāre paribhramati | ebhiś ca hetubhir janmasrotaḥpravṛttir dṛṣṭā hetvabhāvāj janmābhāva iti | tatra ca mokṣakāmaḥ pratibuddhāpratibuddhau vyaktāvyakte ca jānīyāt | etac catuṣṭayam avagamya kṣetrajñaḥ sarvaduḥkhanirmuktaḥ padam akṣaram avāpnotīti |
children.translated_text: <s>Arāḍa</s> said: 'May the greatly fortunate one hear.' He stated: 'The truth concerning <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and its modifications (<s>vikāra</s>) consists of birth, old age, and death. <s>Prakṛti</s> comprises the five great elements, ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), and the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>). The modifications are the senses and their objects. Feet, hands, speech, the organs of excretion and generation, and the mind — this is the field. He who knows this field is called the field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). And the knowers of truth declare the field-knower to be the Self (<s>ātman</s>). That which is subject to birth and cessation, whose nature is death, should be understood as the manifest; the unmanifest is the opposite of this. Ignorance, <s>karma</s>, and craving are to be known as the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s>. The being situated in these three does not transcend existence. The [impediments are]: wrong perception, ego-sense, doubt, confusion, non-discrimination, wrong means, attachment, and downfall. Wrong perception means inverted activity. "I declare," "I know" — such is ego-sense. He who sees even undoubted things as one mass, like a lump of clay, should be considered as [having] doubt. "I myself am those very activities of mind, intellect, and action; this aggregate is I" — they call this confusion. Non-discrimination means the lack of knowledge distinguishing the awakened from the unawakened, the natures themselves — that should be understood as non-discrimination. Oblations with <s>svāhā</s>, with <s>vaṣaṭ</s>, sprinkling, and aspersion — these should be understood as wrong means. When an unintelligent person develops attachment to an object through actions of mind, speech, and intellect — that is called clinging. "This is mine, I belong to this" — the suffering one thus imagines — that is downfall. Laziness is the cause of beings' continued existence. Darkness is delusion; death and birth. Great delusion is called desire. Wrath should be understood as gloom. Despondency is called blind darkness. By this fivefold ignorance, the foolish one, with mind bound, revolves again and again in the great suffering of birth and the rest. There, thinking "I am the seer, the hearer, the thinker, and both cause and effect" — thus he wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>. By these causes, the flow of birth is seen to continue; from the absence of causes comes the absence of birth. There, one desiring liberation should know the awakened and unawakened, the manifest and unmanifest. Having understood this fourfold [truth], the field-knower, freed from all suffering, attains the imperishable state.'
'Having first abandoned the seed that is the bond of worldly existence,
adopting the mark [of renunciation], with desire for pleasure turned away,
content, desiring to attain the supreme state,
embracing pure conduct, one should dwell at the forest's edge.'

children.text: paścāc ca rāgavairāgyaprabhave bhayakṣeme viditvā nigṛhya sarvendriyagrāmaṃ manaḥśamam ālambya tataḥ kāmebhyo viviktaṃ vyāpādādibhyaś ca vivekajaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ savitarkam āpnoti | sa caivaṃvidhena kāmadveṣavigarhiṇā śamenānvito brahmalokam adhigacchati | tāṃś ca vitarkān manaḥsaṃkṣobhakarān avetya tadvirahitaṃ prītisukhātmakaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānam āsādayati | tayā ca prītyā hriyamāṇamanā deveṣv ābhāsvareṣūpapadyate | yaḥ punas tasmāt prītisukhāc cittam uccālayati sa tṛtīyaṃ sukhaprītirahitaṃ dhyānam āpnoti | tat tṛtīyadhyānanimagnamanāś ca śubhakṛtsneṣv amareṣu janma pratilabhate | tādṛśaṃ ca sukham āsādya yo vyapekṣāṃ karoti sa caturthaṃ sukhaduḥkhavirahitaṃ dhyānam upalabhate | tac ca dīrghatvād āyuṣaḥ kecin muktim evādhyavasyanti | kasmāt sukhaduḥkhavicchedāc cetasaś cāvyāpārāt | asya ca dhyānasya bṛhatphalair devaiḥ sāmānyaṃ phalam ācakṣate vidvāṃsaḥ | tasmāc ca samādher vyutthitaḥ śarīriṇāṃ doṣān ālokya śarīravinivṛttihetor jñānam adhigacchati | tad api ca dhyānam apahāya viśeṣakāṅkṣī rūpād api virajyate | yāni cāsmin duḥkhāni śarīre vidyante tāny ādau buddhyā samavalokayaṃs tato ghaneṣv api dravyeṣv ākāśādhimuktim utpādayati | ākāśagataṃ cātmānam abhisaṃkṣipyānantam ākāśam ālokayan viśeṣād adhigamād ātmakauśalād ātmānam ātmani saṃkṣipya kiṃcin nāstīty ākiṃcanya iti saṃjñām upagataḥ śarīravirahān mukta ity abhidhīyate | bodhisattva uvāca |
children.translated_text: 'And afterward, knowing the [pair of] fear and security born from attachment and dispassion, restraining the entire group of senses, taking hold of mental tranquility, one attains the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), born of seclusion from desires and from ill-will and the like, accompanied by initial thought. And endowed with such tranquility that censures desire and hatred, one reaches the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. And recognizing those initial thoughts as disturbers of the mind, one abandons them and attains the second <s>dhyāna</s>, whose nature is joy and happiness. And with the mind carried away by that joy, one is reborn among the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (radiant) gods. And whoever detaches the mind from that joy and happiness attains the third <s>dhyāna</s>, devoid of joy and happiness. And one immersed in the third <s>dhyāna</s> obtains birth among the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (thoroughly good) gods. And having attained such happiness, whoever looks beyond it obtains the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, devoid of both happiness and suffering. And some consider this to be liberation itself, because of the longevity and because of the cessation of happiness and suffering, and because of the mind's non-engagement. The learned declare that this meditation has a common fruit with the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (great-fruited) gods. And one who arises from that concentration, seeing the faults of embodied beings, achieves knowledge aimed at liberation from the body. And abandoning even that meditation, desiring something more, one becomes dispassionate even toward form. And first examining with wisdom the sufferings that exist in this body, one then generates in even solid substances the conviction of space. And concentrating the self perceived as being in space, beholding infinite space, through superior attainment, through self-mastery, concentrating the self within the self, arriving at the designation "there is nothing" — <s>ākiṃcanya</s> (nothingness) — one is said to be liberated through freedom from the body.' The Bodhisattva said:
'If a conscious self still exists,
whence will liberation come?
As long as it exists, there operate
both wholesome and unwholesome actions.'

children.text: yathā ca salilabhūmivirahān na bījaṃ kenacit pravirūḍham ālokitaṃ tatpratyayāc ca dṛṣṭaṃ virohad evam ātmāpi gṛhītavyaḥ | karmājñānatṛṣṇātyāgāc ca yo niścīyate mokṣaḥ sati cātmani tatparityāgam nopalabhāmahe | tadaparityāgāc ca kuto mokṣa ity ahaṃkāraparityāgaś ca saty ātmani kuto bhavet | sati cāhaṃkāre sthitam evedaṃ janmasrotasīty abhidhāya |
children.translated_text: 'Just as a seed, separated from water and earth, is seen by no one sprouting, yet is seen sprouting from those very conditions — so the self too should be understood. And as for the liberation that is determined through the abandonment of <s>karma</s>, ignorance, and craving — as long as the self exists, we do not find the abandonment of these. And without their abandonment, whence liberation? And how could the abandonment of ego-sense come about while the self exists? And as long as ego-sense exists, the stream of birth remains established.' Having spoken thus,
from that hermitage of <s>Arāḍa</s>,
that great-minded one departed,
and by difficult and severe austerities
emaciated his body.

children.text: nānena tapasā tattvādhigamo bhavatīti ca matvotthāya paridurbalaśarīro bodhisattvo nairañjanāyāṃ sariti snātvā sunandāpratipāditaṃ piṇḍam abhyavahṛtya kālena bhujagarājenābhiṣṭutaḥ |
children.translated_text: And thinking 'Truth is not realized by this austerity,' the Bodhisattva arose, his body extremely weak, bathed in the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, ate the alms-food offered by <s>Sunandā</s>, and in time was praised by the serpent-king.
And he was encircled by a [serpent's] body with blue wings
spread in a row of marks, its limbs rosy-hued,
with quivering petals of lotuses —
like a garland mixed with blue lotus leaves.
Then, going with slow steps,
the wise one, radiant as a golden mountain,
beneath the <s>Bodhi</s> tree
sat down for the sake of enlightenment.
Then, together with his daughters,
taking up his floral bow,
<s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid, the mind-born one) came
to agitate his mind.
One, sniffing a fresh <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) flower
before him,
narrowed a certain glance
with a restless pupil.
Another, whispering something
into a friend's ear with a preliminary smile,
that playful beauty
went past, making her face flash coyly.
Another, desirous, displaying herself,
addressed that bull of <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors): 'Look —
a beauty with loosened girdle,
her garment slipping from the hip!'
'Where is this youth, lovely as the moon,
and where your desire for austerity?
Embrace love; turn back from this!
Tell me — what fruit of austerity do you hope to attain?'
'Out of desire for your welfare I speak to you —

children.text: kim ataḥ param āptum icchasi tvam
children.translated_text: what more than this do you wish to obtain?
The great and blameless duty of a householder —

children.text: na vihāya kim anyad asti puṇyam
children.translated_text: what other merit exists apart from abandoning it?'
'Among us who are eager for your embrace, O wise one,
is even this one not beloved, though captivating of heart?' — thus speaking
face to face, that love-stricken woman
was scratching the lotus-faces [of her companions] with her nails.

children.text: yadā ca tāsu bodhisattvaḥ sāvajñam api dṛṣṭiviṣāṇi vikṣipatsv api nānāceṣṭāni darśayatsu dhyānastimitākṣa eva tasthau tadā māraḥ pravyājahāra | bhīṣayitvainam utthāpayateti |

atha bodhisattvasyaivam abhavat | kasmin sati jarāmaraṇaṃ bhavati kiṃ ca pratyayāt | punar evam abhavat | yad utāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ sparśapratyayā vedanā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānam upādānapratyayo bhavo bhavapratyayā jātir jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanty evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ saṃskāranirodhād vijñānanirodho vijñānanirodhān nāmarūpanirodho nāmarūpanirodhāt ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ ṣaḍāyatananirodhāt sparśanirodhaḥ sparśanirodhād vedanānirodho vedanānirodhāt tṛṣṇānirodhas tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodha upādānanirodhād bhavanirodho bhavanirodhāj jātinirodho jātinirodhāj jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante | evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati | ity evaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñācakṣur udapādi |

atha sarvadevagaṇā bodhisattvaṃ bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ prāptābhijñaṃ jitamārabalaṃ jayodgatacchattradhvajapatākaṃ puruṣavaidyaṃ vigatabhayasiṃhaṃ sudāntanāgaṃ traividyaprāptam daśabalavikramaṃ pūrvapraṇidhibodhiprāptaṃ viditvābhisaṃpūjayanta iti prārthayāmāsuḥ |
iti tuṣṭāḥ sarve ca devagaṇāḥ prāñjalayas tatraiva tasthuḥ |
atha tathāgato mahānandaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmīti tataḥ samutthāya carituṃ pracakrāma | atha māro bhagavantaṃ sametyovāca |
atha mārakanyakāḥ pitaraṃ viṣādavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasaitya pratyabhāṣanta |
tatas tāḥ strīcāpalyād aviditaprabhāvā bodhisattvasya prabhūtayauvanamattakāśinyaḥ pitur vacanam anuśrutya bodhisattvam upasaṃkrāntās tanmanaḥ saṃkṣobhayituṃ pracakramire |
tatas tāḥ pitur antikaṃ gatvaivam āhuḥ |
tat sādhu nas tātedam jarājarjaraśarīram antardhāpaya | māra āha |
tatas tās tathāgataṃ prārthayitvā labdhapaurāṇādhikasundaradehāḥ svabhavanaṃ yayuḥ | atha durdine saṃjāte mucilindanāgarājaḥ svabhavanān niṣkramya bhagavataḥ

mā bhūd iti saptabhiḥ phaṇair ācchādya durdine vyatikrānte tathāgataṃ praṇamya svabhavanaṃ jagāma | tataś carakaparivrājakavṛddhaśrāvakagautamanirgranthājīvikādayas taṃ tathāgataṃ nyagrodhamūlasthaṃ praṇipatyocuḥ | api bhagavatā gautamenaitat saptāhadurdinaṃ samyak sukhena vyatināmitam iti | bhagavān āha |

tatas tathāgato dhyānasukhavedī tārāyaṇamūle tasthau | tanmuhūrte trapuṣabhallikau vaṇijau vividhapaṇyaṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāpathād uttarāpathaṃ gacchantau kāṣāyasaṃvṛtaśāntadehaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyantau praharṣajātau tatpādau śirasābhivandya madhupāyasapūrṇapiṇḍapātraṃ tasmai pradadatuḥ | atha tathāgatasya bhojanakālaṃ jñātvā catvāro
saparivārāḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanatūryatāḍāvacarasaṃgītakaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā sarpimaṇḍapātrāṇi prayacchanti sma | atha bhagavāṃs tāni pātrāṇi pratigṛhya maṅgalavākyapūrvaṃ tān uvāca |

children.translated_text: 'May the gods bring well-being to you,
whether standing or going on the path!',
'May your mind always be directed toward <s>Dharma</s>,',
'and never toward sin!'
'May you always be successful,
free from disease, of long life!',
'By this meritorious action, may all Buddhists',
'become sons of the Well-Gone One (<s>Sugata</s>)!'
Hearing these words of the sage,
which illuminated the lotus of the mind,
they forever took refuge
in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>.
Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> had this thought:
'This enlightenment has been attained by me
through extreme difficulty, in the ultimate sense.',
'Even if I were to teach it to others,',
'they would not understand it — enough of that!'
Having thus resolved, the wise sage,
with supreme knowledge, entered into silence.
'One standing in a circle of fools
shines by keeping silence.'

children.text: atha khalu śikhī brāhmaṇas tathāgataraśmisaṃcoditaḥ sārdhaṃ śakrādidevagaṇai rātrau divyāvabhāsenāvabhāsya tathāgatam abhivandya ca dharmadeśanatāyai prārthayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śikhī</s> the Brahmin, impelled by the rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, together with the host of gods headed by <s>Śakra</s>, at night, illuminating [the place] with a divine radiance, having venerated the <s>Tathāgata</s>, entreated him for the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>:
'O Blessed One, in a world blind with delusion,',
'kindle the lamp of wisdom!',
'Upon a world afflicted by hunger and thirst,',
'shower the nectar of the <s>Dharma</s>!'
'Since, having attained enlightenment
austerity,',
only through extreme
'you are absorbed in the pleasures of meditation —',
'this world will [otherwise] go to destruction!'

children.text: atha tathāgatas tam śikhinaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayati sma | tasminn eva samaye māgadhānāṃ pāpācāratvān

children.translated_text: a great portent

children.text: udapādi | punar api śikhī brāhmaṇas tathāgatam etad avocat |
children.translated_text: arose. And again <s>Śikhī</s> the Brahmin said this to the <s>Tathāgata</s>:
Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> consented to <s>Śikhī</s> the Brahmin with silence. At that very time, because of the sinful conduct of the people of <s>Magadha</s>,
'Blessed One, in the land of <s>Magadha</s>,',
'the people are afflicted by great portents,',
'disrupted,',
'troubled by <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>yakṣas</s>!'
'For the pacification of their fire of sin,',
'shower the nectar of the <s>Dharma</s>!',
'Fulfill now',
'what was formerly vowed!'

children.text:
atha bhagavāṃs taṃ sarvāvantaṃ lokadhātuṃ buddhacakṣuṣāvalokayann adhamottamamadhyamāṃ lokasthitiṃ dṛṣṭvā deśayeyaṃ vā na veti vicintayan karuṇayā saṃcoditaḥ śikhine brāhmaṇāya dharmadeśanatayā
svīkṛtavān dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmīti | tataḥ śikhī brāhmaṇaḥ pramuditamanā muneś caraṇau vanditvā svabhavanaṃ yayau | atha bodhivṛkṣadevatā praṇamyaivam āha | kva bhagavan dharmacakraṃ pravartayiṣyasīti | tathāgata āha | vārāṇasyāṃ mṛgadāva iti | kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, surveying the entire world-realm with the Buddha-eye, seeing the inferior, superior, and middling conditions of worldly beings, deliberating 'Shall I teach or not?' — impelled by compassion, he accepted <s>Śikhī</s> the Brahmin's [request] by agreeing to teach the <s>Dharma</s>: 'I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s>!' Then <s>Śikhī</s> the Brahmin, his mind delighted, having venerated the sage's feet, went to his own dwelling. Then the deity of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, having bowed, spoke thus: 'Where, Blessed One, will you turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel?' The <s>Tathāgata</s> said: 'In the Deer Park at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.' Why?
'<s>Kāśī</s> is a blessed land,',
'abundant in provisions, a refuge of good people,',
'where the gods, though immortal, always dwell',
'with the wish to become mortal [there].'
Moreover:
'There the wheel was turned',
'by former Buddhas, <s>Tathāgatas</s>;',
'and those yet to come will also turn',
'the <s>Dharma</s> [-wheel] in that very place.'

children.text: tato vārāṇasīṃ gamiṣyāmīti prasthitaṃ tathāgatam ājīvako dṛṣṭvā praṇāmaṃ kṛtavān | tenaiva sārdhaṃ vividhāṃ saṃmodanāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā bhagavataḥ kva gamanābhiprāyam ity abhyanuyuktas tathagataś cainam avocat |
children.translated_text: Then, as the <s>Tathāgata</s> set out to go to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, an <s>Ājīvaka</s> [ascetic], seeing him, made obeisance. Having exchanged various pleasant conversations with him, and being asked about the Blessed One's intended destination, the <s>Tathāgata</s> said to him:
'I shall go to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,',
'of yogins,',
'having reached the city',
'I shall kindle the torch of <s>Dharma</s>',
'for the world that has become blind!'

children.text: gaccha gautamety utthāya sa ājīvako dakṣiṇābhimukhaḥ prakrāntaḥ | tathāgato 'pi vārāṇasīm abhigacchan gaṅgāmahānadīṃ vihāyasā tīrtvānupūrveṇa janapadacārikāṃ caran pātracīvaram ādāya vārāṇasīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat | tasyāṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhakta ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve devatābhiḥ prajñaptaratnasiṃhāsane paryaṅkam ābhujya samādhistimitavigrahas tasthau | tataḥ pañcakā bhadravargīyā bhikṣavas tathāgatasya pādau śirobhir

children.translated_text: bowing,

children.text: prāñjalayo niṣeduḥ | atha tathāgatadehād raśmir niścaran sarvāvantaṃ lokadhātum avabhāsya saṃcodayati sma |
children.translated_text: sat with folded hands. Then a ray emanating from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, illuminating the entire world-realm, urged [all beings] thus:

'Go, O <s>Gautama</s>!' — saying this, the <s>Ājīvaka</s>, rising, departed southward. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, proceeding toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, having crossed the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s> through the sky, gradually wandering through the countryside, taking bowl and robe, entered the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms. Having wandered for alms in that [city] and having eaten, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Deer Park), on a jewel-lion-throne prepared by the deities, sitting cross-legged, his body stilled in <s>samādhi</s>, he remained. Then the five monks of the auspicious group, venerating the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet with their heads,
'Having obtained the rare human birth,',
'the conjunction of favorable moments is extremely rare.',
'And the arising of a <s>Tathāgata</s>',
'is as rare as the <s>udumbara</s> flower!'
'Today the <s>Buddha</s> has gone to <s>Kāśī</s>',
'for the pacification of the suffering of the world.',
'Therefore let your mind be directed toward the <s>Dharma</s> —',
'come here swiftly!'

children.text:
tataḥ samantād digbhyaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānasamanvāgatā bodhisattvagaṇāḥ
śakrabrahmādilokapālāḥ surāsurayakṣagandharvagaruḍakinnaramahoraganāgarājamanuṣyāś ca svasvabhavanād āgatya tathāgatasya mahatīṃ pūjāṃ prakurvantaś caraṇayor nipatya bhagavantam abhisaṃmukhās tatraiva tasthuḥ | tato dharmacakrapravartano nāma bodhisattvo bhagavantaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇamya sarvaratnamayaṃ sahasrāraṃ nānāsugandhipuṣpadāmasaṃyuktaṃ tathāgatapūjārtham upanāmayya kṛtāñjalipuṭo dharmacakrapravartanāyainaṃ prārthayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, from all directions, hosts of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with former aspirations, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other world-guardians, gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>nāga</s>-kings, and humans — coming from their respective abodes, performing great worship to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, falling at his feet, facing the Blessed One, stood there. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dharmacakrapravartana</s> ('Turner of the Dharma-Wheel'), having circumambulated the Blessed One and bowed, offering for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> a thousand-spoked [wheel] made of all kinds of gems, adorned with garlands of various fragrant flowers, with folded hands entreated him to turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel:
'O Blessed One, tiger among sages,',
'conqueror of <s>Māra</s>, bull among the victorious!',
'Fill the conch-shell of <s>Dharma</s>,',
'for the terror of the deer of false doctrines!'
'You who formerly, in the beginning, made',
'the vow:',
'"I shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the worlds',
'for the pacification of the suffering of beings" —'
'Fulfill, O Blessed One, O Protector,',
'the completion of that vow!',
'For if the Blessed One, the Teacher, [does not teach],',
'the world [will remain] troubled by the suffering of existence!'
'By the grace of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>,',
'you now become the <s>Buddha</s>.',
'Seeing the world ablaze with the fire of suffering,',
'shower the nectar [of the <s>Dharma</s>]!'
'<s>Brahmā</s> and the other world-guardians',
'have come, desiring to hear.',
'For the destruction of the root of suffering,',
'turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel!'
Then spoke the great Buddhist,
the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, ocean of compassion,
surveying the assembly
and addressing the five monks:
'Born from the seed of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>),',
'the sprout of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) grows.',
'Drinking the sap of merit and demerit,',
'it becomes the great tree of existence (<s>bhava</s>).'
'Its fruit is great and sweet [at first],',
'but its ripening becomes poison.',
'Therefore, knowing it to be a poison-fruit,',
'it should be abandoned from afar by the wise.'
'To burn the sprout of the poison-tree,',
'let the seed itself be burned!',
'is burned,',
'When the seed of ignorance',
'liberation from existence is certain!'
Thus the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>,
the charioteer of those to be tamed,
having turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel,
then taught the <s>Dharma</s> further:
The Four Noble Truths for <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers),
the Noble Eightfold Path,
the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) that is auspicious
in the beginning, end, and middle.
Then the earth trembled, with its mountains and oceans,
its garment the still ocean, as if from joy;
the divine drum-sounds spread through the sky;
the directions shone, adorned with serenity.
The clouds from all sides, gently thundering, laughing,
fastened with lightning —
with pollen scattered from their mutual embrace,
continuously showered flowers upon him.
The breeze, moving with steady pace,
carrying the fragrant pollen born from various tree-blossoms,
with undivided devotion set in motion by joy,
worshipped him as if with fine cloth-offerings.
in the entire world-realm,
Then,
there arose practitioners of the holy life,
who, having heard the word of the <s>Buddha</s>,
became devoted to the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>.
Then all, having risen,
performed worship to the teacher of the world,
and saying 'Today the world has a protector!' —
departed with joy.

children.text: iti | eṣa rājakumāro rājyasukhatṛpto divyastrīparibhogavirataḥ sakalarājyabhogyāni tṛṇavad vijahya paraduḥkhena duḥkhī duṣkaracaryāṃ caran balavantaṃ māraṃ
children.translated_text: This royal prince, satiated with the pleasures of kingship, having ceased from the enjoyment of divine women, having abandoned all royal enjoyments as if they were grass, suffering from the suffering of others, practicing difficult austerities, having conquered the mighty <s>Māra</s>,
conquering [him],

children.text: samyaksaṃbodhim api prāpto buddho babhūva | ayam eva bhagavāñ chākyasiṃhas tribhuvananātha iti bodhigaveṣiṇā puruṣeṇa rājyasukham api viramaṇīyam | duṣkareṇāpi bhavitavyaṃ māram api jetavyam iti bodhisattvena bodhivāñchayā bhavitavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: he attained supreme perfect enlightenment and became the <s>Buddha</s>. This very Blessed One, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the lord of the three worlds — therefore, by a man who seeks enlightenment, even royal happiness should be renounced; one must endure even the most difficult things; even <s>Māra</s> must be conquered — thus, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> must have the aspiration for enlightenment.

And the Blessed One too, thinking 'I shall effect the deliverance of all beings,' arose and wandered through the countryside. Thus, this Blessed One, out of desire for the welfare of the three worlds, having abandoned even divine happiness, performed what is difficult to do — therefore the highest faith should be placed in the <s>Buddha</s>. And his <s>Dharma</s> should be heard with reverence, [knowing that] he attained enlightenment through such extreme
|| Thus ends the <s>Śākyasiṃha-tathāgata Jātaka</s> (The Birth-Story of the Lion of the Śākyas, the Tathāgata). ||
